prompt_text:
Task: Managed Log Query / Log Ingestion

Write code that retrieves recent log results filtered by field values and time range using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon CloudWatch Logs:
  Service: Amazon CloudWatch Logs
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: put_log_events, filter_log_events, start_query
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_PutLogEvents.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_StartQuery.html

Option 2 — Azure Monitor Logs:
  Service: Azure Monitor Logs / Logs Ingestion API
  SDK: azure-monitor-ingestion / azure-monitor-query
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: upload, query_workspace, query_resource
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/custom-logs-overview, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/api/overview

Option 3 — Datadog:
  Service: Datadog Logs API
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: submit logs, search logs
  Setup hints: DD_API_KEY, DD_APP_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/guide/access-your-log-data-programmatically/, https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/logs/

Option 4 — IBM Cloud Logs:
  Service: IBM Cloud Logs
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /logs/v1/singles, query data, DataPrime filters
  Setup hints: IBM_CLOUD_API_KEY, IBM_LOGS_INSTANCE_ID, IBM_LOGS_REGION
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/products/cloud-logs

Option 5 — Alibaba Simple Log Service:
  Service: Simple Log Service
  SDK: aliyun-log-python-sdk
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: PutLogs, GetLogs, GetLogsV2
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET, ALIBABA_SLS_ENDPOINT
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2847535.html, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2771313.html

Option 6 — Google Cloud Logging:
  Service: Cloud Logging
  SDK: google-cloud-logging
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: entries.write, entries.list
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/entries/write, https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/entries/list

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import boto3
import time
import os

def get_recent_logs(log_group_name: str, start_time_ms: int, end_time_ms: int, filter_field: str, filter_value: str) -> list:
    """
    Retrieves recent log results from Amazon CloudWatch Logs, filtered by a field value and time range.

    Args:
        log_group_name: The name of the CloudWatch Log Group.
        start_time_ms: The start of the time range in milliseconds since epoch.
        end_time_ms: The end of the time range in milliseconds since epoch.
        filter_field: The log field to filter by (e.g., 'level').
        filter_value: The value to match for the filter_field (e.g., 'ERROR').

    Returns:
        A list of dictionaries, where each dictionary represents a log entry.
    """
    # Initialize AWS CloudWatch Logs client
    # AWS_REGION environment variable or default 'us-east-1' is used.
    # AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are expected to be set
    # in the environment or configured via AWS credentials file.
    client = boto3.client('logs', region_name=os.environ.get('AWS_REGION', 'us-east-1'))

    # Construct the CloudWatch Logs Insights query string
    # This query selects timestamp and message, filters by the specified field and value,
    # and sorts the results by timestamp in descending order.
    query_string = f"fields @timestamp, @message | filter {filter_field} = '{filter_value}' | sort @timestamp desc"

    # Start the query in CloudWatch Logs
    start_query_response = client.start_query(
        logGroupName=log_group_name,
        startTime=start_time_ms,
        endTime=end_time_ms,
        queryString=query_string,
        limit=100  # Maximum number of log events to return for this query
    )

    query_id = start_query_response['queryId']
    
    # Poll for query results until the query completes or fails
    response = None
    while response is None or response['status'] not in ['Complete', 'Failed', 'Cancelled', 'Timeout']:
        time.sleep(1) # Wait for 1 second before polling again
        response = client.get_query_results(
            queryId=query_id
        )
    
    results = []
    if response['status'] == 'Complete':
        # Parse the results into a list of dictionaries
        for record in response['results']:
            log_entry = {}
            for field in record:
                log_entry[field['field']] = field['value']
            results.append(log_entry)
    else:
        # Handle cases where the query did not complete successfully
        print(f"CloudWatch Logs Insights query did not complete. Status: {response['status']}")
    
    return results
